significance: A coastal-country shrine of Pudukkottai district counted as the seventh of the Pandya-region Tevara sthalams, where Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar each sang the presiding deity.
story: The four Vedas together with Brahma, Vishnu and Lakshmi, Indra, Surya, Chandra and the sages Vasishta and Agastya are all said to have worshipped Shiva here.
